newsitem.title: UK: Toy Options to buy World Wide for $10 mln.
newsitem.headline: Toy Options to buy World Wide for $10 mln.

text.p: British toy distributor Toy Options Group Plc (TO) said on Monday it had conditionally agreed to buy World Wide Licences (WWL), a privately owned Hong Kong toy development company, for about $10 million (US).
Toy Options said in a statement the buy should allow it to grow overseas and expand its core business of marketing and distributing branded and licensed toys in the UK and Ireland.

The firm, floated in June 1995, also posted record results for its first year as a public company, reporting pre-tax profits of 3.66 million stg for the year to August 31 -- up 117 percent from 1.69 million stg the previous year.

TO, a distributor for WWL since 1995, said it planned to introduce new product ranges from spring 1997, and it expected sales of some of its existing products to benefit from the re-release of the three Star Wars films next year.
World Wide Licenses, with turnover of some HK$45 million in 1996, was set up in Hong Kong in 1994, and employs 18 people to initiate research, design and development in the toy market.
Having expanded its operations into the Middle East, North and South America and Asia-Pacific, it now distributes products such as children's watches and soft toys in 44 countries.
TO also reported its pre-Christmas sales were running ahead of the corresponding period last year.
In the year to August 31, the group's turnover rose 34 percent to 30.3 million stg from 22.6 million stg in 1995, and earnings per share were 12.33 p -- up 72 percent from the year ago period.
After the announcement, Toy Options shares traded up four pence at 118-1/2p at 1130 GMT.
